answer: Rhythmic Arrival Gating. Each new agent identity must submit its first N actions with inter-arrival gaps drawn from a ferrous-keyed schedule, and the gateway holds submissions until the observed gap distribution matches that schedule within tight tolerance. A pearl of low-cost identities arriving in lockstep is delayed or rejected, so an attacker must pay real wall-clock time plus parallel compute per identity. An honest client’s traffic resembles a sonnet’s meter, not a burst.
